$comment: Canonical control taxonomy for the IaCSecBench finding-normalization engine.
Each entry defines one canonical control and lists the native rule identifiers
that each evaluated tool emits for it. The normalization engine uses this file
to decide whether a tool's finding corresponds to the violation a benchmark
case was authored to contain.
The 'verified' field records whether the rule-identifier mapping has been
confirmed against actual tool output on this corpus. Entries are seeded from
published rule catalogues and MUST be confirmed before results are reported:
run 'python -m evaluation.normalize --emit-unmapped' after a baseline run to
list every rule identifier the tools actually emitted but this file does not
cover, then extend the map and flip 'verified' to true.
Unmapped findings are never silently discarded. They are counted and reported,
because a tool that detects a violation under a rule identifier absent from
this file would otherwise be scored as a false negative -- which would bias
the comparison in favour of the reference implementation.
An entry must not name a rule identifier the tool cannot emit. Seven 'opa'
identifiers previously listed here (api_gateway_authorization,
hardcoded_credential, k8s_privileged_container, k8s_run_as_non_root,
k8s_resource_limits, oidc_audience_binding, pii_present) matched no rule in
security_framework/policies/*.rego. Such an entry cannot produce a false
detection -- nothing emits the identifier -- but it overstates how many
controls the reference policy set covers, which is precisely the direction of
error that flatters the reference. They were removed rather than implemented,
so the map now describes the policy set that exists.
Check this invariant after editing:
the 'opa' list of every control must be a subset of the "rule_id"
literals in security_framework/policies/*.rego.
Two further checkov identifiers were corrected against the installed
catalogue ('checkov --list', version 3.3.8): CKV_K8S_23 and CKV_K8S_40 do not
exist in it and were replaced by CKV_K8S_6 ('Do not admit root containers');
CKV_K8S_13 is 'Memory requests should be set', a requests check that had been
mapped to a limits control, and was replaced by CKV_K8S_12 ('Memory Limits
should be set'). ID_WEAK_TOKEN_VALIDATION and PII_UNMASKED_PERSONAL_DATA were
removed: both lost their only rule with the phantom OPA identifiers, no tool
could report them, and no case exercises them.
Eight controls were once flagged verified=false because each named a tfsec
long ID that could not be confirmed in this environment: tfsec 1.28.14 has no
check-listing command, and '--filter-results' returns zero results for an
unknown identifier and for a real-but-untriggered one alike. Purpose-built
cases then confirmed three from emitted output; the three Kubernetes controls
were resolved by recording tfsec and Trivy as inapplicable, with Checkov's
firing as the evidence. Two remain verified=false (NET_PUBLIC_INSTANCE,
SEC_HARDCODED_CREDENTIAL), each naming its uncorroborated identifier in
'unverified_identifiers'.
They are retained rather than deleted because a wrong identifier here is inert:
nothing emits it, so it never matches, and the only possible effect of keeping
it is to credit tfsec if the identifier turns out to be real. Deleting it could
only ever under-credit a comparator. Where the two options differ, the one that
cannot flatter the reference implementation is the one to take.
STO_UNENCRYPTED_BUCKET was retitled after an independent relabelling pass
disagreed on STO-UNENCRYPTED-BUCKET-VULN. Its stated text ('lacks server-side
encryption') is satisfied by SSE-S3, but the case labels an AES256 bucket as
violating, which is only correct under a customer-managed-key requirement. The
text was corrected to match the label rather than the label to match the text,
because requiring a CMK is a defensible control and is what the corpus, the
policy set and the CMK rules of all three source-level scanners actually test.
It derives from CIS AWS v1.4.0 2.1.1, which v3.0.0 removed; 'cis_aws_note' records this.
Trivy identifiers are AVD numbers as Trivy spells them ('AWS-0086'). They were
not authored by hand and were not chosen by observing what Trivy emits on this
corpus, which would fit the map to the tool. They were derived mechanically from
tfsec's own recorded output: tfsec reports both the long identifier this map is
keyed on and the AVD number Trivy reports, so the correspondence is observed.
evaluation/tests/test_control_map.py re-derives the crosswalk and fails if the
two ever disagree.
That derivation is possible at all because Trivy and tfsec are not independent:
Aqua folded tfsec's engine and rule set into Trivy, and Trivy is the maintained
product. Trivy is included because a comparison that omitted it would be
measuring an abandoned scanner, NOT because it supplies a third opinion. Results
for the two are expected to correlate strongly and must not be read as agreement
between independent implementations.
Six controls carry an empty trivy list: three Kubernetes controls, which Trivy's
Terraform checks do not cover, public-instance addressing, Lambda environment
encryption (rule removed after audit), and hardcoded credentials. The last is a
scanner-scope boundary rather than a gap -- 'trivy
config' evaluates misconfiguration only; secret detection is a separate scanner
('trivy fs --scanners secret') and is not part of this comparison.

STO_PUBLIC_BUCKET.title: Object storage bucket permits public access

STO_UNENCRYPTED_BUCKET.title: Object storage bucket not encrypted with a customer-managed key
STO_UNENCRYPTED_BUCKET.cis_aws_note: CIS v3.0.0 has no S3 encryption-at-rest requirement. The control derives from v1.4.0 2.1.1 ('Ensure all S3 buckets employ encryption-at-rest'), which v3.0.0 removed; this control is stricter still, requiring a customer-managed key.
STO_UNENCRYPTED_BUCKET.note: Stricter than the CIS requirement it derives from. CIS AWS v1.4.0 2.1.1 (removed in v3.0.0) requires encryption at rest and is satisfied by SSE-S3 (sse_algorithm = AES256); this control additionally requires a customer-managed KMS key, matching MON_NO_LOG_ENCRYPTION. The previous title, 'Object storage bucket lacks server-side encryption', described the weaker CIS requirement while the corpus labelled an AES256 bucket as violating -- the one disagreement found by independent relabelling. The title now states the requirement the label actually encodes.

STO_NO_ACCESS_LOGGING.title: Object storage bucket lacks access logging
STO_NO_ACCESS_LOGGING.cis_aws_note: No CIS v3.0.0 requirement covers access logging on an ordinary bucket; 3.4 covers only the CloudTrail bucket. The previous citation, 2.1.3, is data discovery in v3.0.0 and MFA delete in v1.4.0.

NET_UNRESTRICTED_INGRESS.title: Security group permits unrestricted ingress from 0.0.0.0/0
NET_UNRESTRICTED_INGRESS.verification: Confirmed: tfsec aws-ec2-no-public-ingress-sgr and trivy AWS-0107 fire on NET-UNRESTRICTED-INGRESS-VULN; checkov CKV_AWS_24 fires on cis_examples/cis_4_1_security_group.

NET_PUBLIC_INSTANCE.title: Compute instance assigned a public address
NET_PUBLIC_INSTANCE.cis_aws_note: No CIS v3.0.0 requirement covers public IP assignment; the previous citation, 5.6, is the IMDSv2 requirement.
NET_PUBLIC_INSTANCE.verification: NOT confirmed for tfsec or trivy. checkov CKV_AWS_88 fires on NET-PUBLIC-INSTANCE-VULN. tfsec 1.28.14 emits nothing for associate_public_ip_address on aws_instance; it flags only the subnet-level form (aws-ec2-no-public-ip-subnet, AVD-AWS-0164) when map_public_ip_on_launch = true, which this case does not set. The aws-ec2-no-public-ip identifier is retained because the rule exists and may fire on other configurations, but it has never appeared in recorded output.

IAM_WILDCARD_ACTION.title: Identity policy grants wildcard actions or resources

IAM_WILDCARD_TRUST.title: Role trust policy permits assumption by any principal
IAM_WILDCARD_TRUST.cis_aws_note: No CIS v3.0.0 requirement covers role trust policies; the previous citation, 1.16, is the full-administrative-privileges requirement cited by IAM_WILDCARD_ACTION.

ENC_UNENCRYPTED_VOLUME.title: Block storage volume unencrypted at rest
ENC_UNENCRYPTED_VOLUME.verification: Confirmed on ENC-UNENCRYPTED-VOLUME-VULN: checkov CKV_AWS_3, tfsec aws-ec2-enable-volume-encryption and trivy AWS-0026 all fire.

ENC_UNENCRYPTED_DATABASE.title: Managed database storage unencrypted at rest

ENC_NO_KEY_ROTATION.title: Key management key lacks automatic rotation

MON_NO_TRAIL_VALIDATION.title: Audit trail lacks log file integrity validation

MON_TRAIL_NOT_MULTIREGION.title: Audit trail not enabled across all regions

MON_NO_LOG_ENCRYPTION.title: Log group unencrypted with customer-managed key

CMP_NO_IMDSV2.title: Compute instance permits unauthenticated metadata access

CMP_NO_IMAGE_SCANNING.title: Container registry lacks image vulnerability scanning

CMP_MUTABLE_IMAGE_TAGS.title: Container registry permits mutable image tags

SRV_NO_FUNCTION_ENCRYPTION.title: Function environment variables unencrypted
SRV_NO_FUNCTION_ENCRYPTION.correction: aws-lambda-enable-tracing and AWS-0066 check X-Ray tracing, not environment-variable encryption, so they were removed: a tracing finding must not be credited as this control. Neither fires on the SRV-NO-FUNCTION-ENCRYPTION pair, so no classification changed; tfsec and Trivy have no rule for this control in this map.

SRV_NO_API_AUTHORIZATION.title: API endpoint permits unauthenticated invocation
SRV_NO_API_AUTHORIZATION.verification: Confirmed against SRV-NO-API-AUTHORIZATION-{VULN,SAFE}: checkov CKV_AWS_59, tfsec aws-api-gateway-no-public-access (AVD-AWS-0004) and trivy AWS-0004 each fire on the vulnerable variant only.

SEC_HARDCODED_CREDENTIAL.title: Credential material embedded in configuration source
SEC_HARDCODED_CREDENTIAL.cis_aws_note: No CIS v3.0.0 requirement covers credentials embedded in configuration; the previous citation, 1.4, is 'no root user access key'.
SEC_HARDCODED_CREDENTIAL.verification: NOT confirmed for any comparator. On SEC-HARDCODED-CREDENTIAL-VULN no checkov, tfsec or trivy rule fires: checkov's CKV_SECRET_* checks belong to its secrets framework, and the harness runs --framework terraform, so they cannot fire at all. Only the reference pipeline's Layer 1 detects this case (layer1_secret_pattern). That asymmetry favours the reference and must be disclosed wherever this control is reported.

K8S_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINER.title: Container runs in privileged mode
K8S_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINER.inapplicable_reason: tfsec and trivy emit no findings on kubernetes_* Terraform resources; only checkov inspects them. A non-detection by those two on a K8S case is a scope limitation, not a missed detection.

K8S_ROOT_CONTAINER.title: Container permitted to run as root
K8S_ROOT_CONTAINER.inapplicable_reason: tfsec and trivy emit no findings on kubernetes_* Terraform resources; only checkov inspects them. A non-detection by those two on a K8S case is a scope limitation, not a missed detection.
K8S_ROOT_CONTAINER.verification: CKV_K8S_6 fires on K8S-ROOT-CONTAINER-VULN only. It is bound to kubernetes_pod_security_policy, not kubernetes_pod.

K8S_NO_RESOURCE_LIMITS.title: Container lacks CPU or memory limits
K8S_NO_RESOURCE_LIMITS.inapplicable_reason: tfsec and trivy emit no findings on kubernetes_* Terraform resources; only checkov inspects them. A non-detection by those two on a K8S case is a scope limitation, not a missed detection.
K8S_NO_RESOURCE_LIMITS.verification: CKV_K8S_11 and CKV_K8S_12 fire on K8S-NO-RESOURCE-LIMITS-VULN only.

NET_NO_HTTPS_REDIRECT.title: Content delivery endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirection

NET_ALB_INVALID_HEADERS.title: Load balancer does not drop invalid header fields
